title: arXiv Trending Physics — Daily — 2026-10-01
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper selection from a very fresh batch with sparse citation/popularity evidence; the ordering is not a measured readership ranking.

sections.title: Quantization through Dissipation and the Optical Quantum Hall Effect
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: The authors combine terahertz Faraday-rotation measurements and numerical analysis to argue that a low-frequency dissipative contribution from impurity states is needed to recover quantized Hall response from the finite-frequency spectrum.
sections.claimed_result: In two GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron-gas samples, the cyclotron-resonance spectrum alone does not reproduce quantized plateaus under a Kramers–Kronig transform; adding a faint, low-frequency impurity-state contribution does.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental and computational; THz Faraday rotation and DC transport on two GaAs/AlGaAs 2DEGs, supported by numerical analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: The measurements cover two samples and specific temperatures/disorder conditions; the proposed mechanism's generality beyond these 2DEGs remains to be tested.

sections.title: Topological Fermi-polaron Polaritons with Electrically Invertible Topology
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: The authors report a gate-controlled semiconductor–photonic-crystal platform in which Fermi-polaron interactions create topological polariton bands whose gap and topology can be electrically tuned and inverted.
sections.claimed_result: In a gated MoSe2 monolayer coupled to a symmetry-engineered photonic crystal, the authors demonstrate electrically invertible topological gaps, Berry curvature and Chern number, with interaction-enhanced time-reversal-symmetry breaking; full text reports gaps up to about 4 meV at 7 T.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; gate-controlled MoSe2/photonic-crystal device with optical measurements of polariton bands.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a platform demonstration in a particular material/device architecture; robustness, scaling and useful chiral-edge transport in larger circuits remain open.

sections.title: Is DESI Seeing Dynamical Dark Energy, or a Cosmic Glitch in Gravity?
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: Combining DESI DR2 baryon-acoustic-oscillation and CMB data, the authors find that a one-parameter model with weaker cosmological gravity fits at least as well as a two-parameter dynamical-dark-energy model.
sections.claimed_result: The fitted ratio is G_cosmo/G_N = 0.9920 ± 0.0025; the authors report a 3.3σ preference and say the one-parameter model predicts DESI distances when fit to CMB data alone.
sections.evidence_type: Observational-data analysis and theoretical model comparison; Planck, ACT, SPT, DESI DR2, with additional CMB-lensing and supernova tests.
sections.unique_caveat: A 3.3σ preference within a specified model/data analysis is not a discovery of modified gravity; the conclusion remains conditional on the model, likelihoods and dataset treatment.

sections.title: Improved Constraints on Cosmic Microwave Background Circular Polarization with CLASS
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: Using CLASS measurements at 90, 150 and 220 GHz alongside prior 40 GHz data, the team tightens CMB circular-polarization limits and reports the first limits on the temperature–circular-polarization spectrum.
sections.claimed_result: Both VV and TV spectra are consistent with zero; the paper gives 95% upper limits of 5.4×10^-3 μK_CMB^2 for VV at 10<ℓ<30 and 5.8×10^-1 μK_CMB^2 for TV at 30<ℓ<50.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; CLASS 40, 90, 150 and 220 GHz data, combined with Planck temperature data for TV.
sections.unique_caveat: These are upper limits, not a detection; the analysis explicitly compares the atmospheric circular-polarization spectrum, so residual atmosphere and instrumental systematics remain relevant.

sections.title: Probing the Reionization History and Bubble Sizes with JWST Lyman-α Fraction Measurements
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: The authors compare JWST Lyman-α emitter fractions at redshifts roughly 6–14 with THESAN simulations and semi-analytic transmission models to constrain reionization and ionized-bubble sizes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report good fit to current JWST fractions and infer mass-weighted neutral fractions at z≈7, 8 and 11; depending on the Lyman-α equivalent-width threshold, central estimates range from 0.38/0.52 at z≈7 to 0.93/0.89 at z≈11.
sections.evidence_type: Observational-data interpretation plus computational modeling; JWST Lyman-α fractions compared with THESAN and semi-analytic transmission calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: Inferences are model-dependent and calibrated using empirical intrinsic Lyman-α equivalent-width distributions near z≈6; the reported 1σ intervals are broad and asymmetric, especially at lower redshift.

sections.title: When Streams Curve Away: a Test of Dark Matter from Extragalactic Stellar Stream Populations
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: The authors propose a geometry-only diagnostic of projected stellar streams that could statistically distinguish halo-shape populations expected under collisionless cold dark matter and self-interacting dark matter.
sections.claimed_result: The authors forecast that survey-scale catalogs of stream morphology could separate CDM and SIDM predictions at up to 5σ using the rate of segments whose curvature points away from the host center.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational forecast; geometric diagnostic and projected stellar-stream populations.
sections.unique_caveat: The 5σ figure is a forecast, not a present measurement; it depends on future survey-scale samples and on controlling projection, selection and halo-model effects.

sections.title: Interpreting the High-Recoil LUX-ZEPLIN Event with Bino-/Singlino-like and Higgsino Dark Matter
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: The authors examine two supersymmetric dark-matter explanations for a reported LZ nuclear-recoil candidate near 248 keV and derive distinct recoil-spectrum expectations.
sections.claimed_result: The paper presents elastic bino/singlino-like and inelastic Higgsino scenarios for the candidate; its example NMSSM benchmark lies below current LZ limits.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical phenomenology; model calculations for supersymmetric neutralinos, relic abundance and direct-detection recoil spectra.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model interpretation of a single candidate event, not evidence that dark matter has been detected; the authors note strong constraints on the minimal thermal inelastic realization from solar-neutrino searches.

sections.title: All Unitaries Have Constant Depth Quantum Circuits
sections.published: 2026-09-30 (date only; UTC clock time unavailable from arXiv abstract page)
sections.abstract: The authors show that any n-qubit unitary can be approximated in polynomial circuit depth using exponentially many ancillas, or in constant depth when unbounded-fan-out gates are allowed.
sections.claimed_result: For error ε, the authors give one- and two-qubit circuits of depth poly(n, log(1/ε)) using 2^O(n) ancillas; unbounded fan-out reduces the depth further to constant.
sections.unique_caveat: The depth reduction trades against exponential ancilla count, and the constant-depth version assumes an unbounded-fan-out gate model; this is not a practical near-term circuit claim.
